title:
Dividend Policy and the Trade-Off Between Real and Accrual-Based Earnings Management:
Empirical Evidence from the KOSPI Market
content:
In this study, we examine whether dividend policy is associated evenly with accrual-based and real operating
earnings-management measures. We analyze 8,839 firm-year observations from 569 non-financial firms listed in the
Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) market from 1996 to 2024 using firm and year fixed-effects regressions
with firm-clustered standard errors. We find no consistent association between dividend yield and accrual-based
manipulation, but we find a negative association with abnormal operating-cash-flow manipulation. As dividend yield
rises, the within-firm relation between the two measures becomes weaker, especially when dividends absorb a large
share of operating profit. Free-cash-flow and operating-cash-flow results point in the same direction, although both
measures share an operating-cash-flow component with the outcome. Cash holdings provide suggestive conditioning
evidence, ownership concentration has no reliable moderating role, and our chaebol result is statistically inconclusive
because the affiliated sample is small. Alternative real-activity measures do not reproduce our core result, so our
evidence is concentrated in abnormal operating cash flow. Boards and regulators should assess dividends together
with accrual and operating-cash-flow indicators, especially when payouts absorb a large share of internal resources.
